title: U.S. House · New York's 26th District
area: Western New York, including Buffalo and most of Erie County, plus Niagara Falls and part of Niagara County.

context.text: Both the Democratic and Republican/Conservative primaries for this seat were canceled; incumbent Timothy M. Kennedy and Dennis Hannon each advanced without appearing on a primary ballot.

summary.text: Timothy M. Kennedy is the Democratic incumbent, a licensed occupational therapist and former Erie County legislator and NY State Senator who won a 2024 special election to the House. He serves on the Homeland Security and Veterans' Affairs committees and is seeking a first full term.

background.text: Born in Buffalo, New York in 1976; earned bachelor's and master's degrees in occupational therapy from D'Youville College in 1999.
Worked as a licensed occupational therapist before entering public office.
Served on the Erie County legislature from 2004 to 2010 and in the New York State Senate from 2011 to 2024.

positions.summary: His official site says he is advocating legislation to ban assault weapons, pass universal background checks, strengthen red flag laws and prohibit sales of ghost guns and high-capacity ammunition.
positions.quote: Ban assault weapons and modifiers, including bump stocks Pass universal background checks for all firearm purchases Strengthen red flag laws Prohibit the sale of ghost guns and high-capacity ammunition

positions.summary: His official site lists protecting and expanding the Affordable Care Act among his healthcare goals.
positions.quote: Protect and expand the Affordable Care Act

positions.summary: His official site says he worked to protect reproductive rights in New York, including codifying Roe v. Wade, and is committed to leading that fight in Congress.
positions.quote: In New York, Kennedy has worked to protect reproductive rights and is committed to leading that fight at the national level in Congress.

positions.summary: His official site criticizes the Trump administration's expansion of immigration enforcement tactics, says he voted against unchecked ICE funding and supports bills such as the Freeze ICE Act.
positions.quote: Voted against unchecked funding for ICE

positions.summary: In an April 2026 statement on the war in Iran, he says the war began without a vote of Congress and calls on the Speaker to bring a war powers resolution to the House floor.
positions.quote: I call on Congressional Republicans to put our nation above their fear of President Trump and finally exercise the authority they have under the Constitution. Speaker Johnson must immediately bring a war powers resolution to the House Floor to bring an end to this illegal war and rein in this dangerous and delusional president.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Homeland Security (Emergency Management and Technology; Transportation and Maritime Security subcommittees) and the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs (Economic Opportunity; Oversight and Investigations subcommittees) in the 119th Congress.

Introduced H.R. 9382, requiring U.S. Customs and Border Protection to link together family members' applications throughout the NEXUS trusted-traveler application process; the bill passed the House on September 16, 2026 and was sent to the Senate.

summary.text: Dennis Hannon is a technology professional and first-time candidate running as the Republican and Conservative nominee, with a campaign centered on public safety, lowering costs and child-protection policy.

background.text: Grew up working in his father's construction business.

priorities.text: Public safety, including strengthening cooperation between local and federal agencies, enforcing immigration and worksite laws, and cracking down on fentanyl trafficking.
Lowering costs, including tax relief for working-class families and lower prescription drug and healthcare costs, especially for seniors.
Child-protection policy, including online privacy protections for minors and opposing gender-affirming medical care for minors.
